<reason>A won by keeping a cleaner vote comparison: the status-quo subsidy is live now, a portable floor can close it without full reclassification, and CON’s decoupling alternative is unscheduled. B landed real mechanical pressure on timing, thresholds, and compliance, but the rationing story had to be rewritten after A’s Q2, and “specify every parameter now or reject the floor” never outweighed A’s ordinary social-insurance answers (trailing lookback, public remittance, days-not-years). B’s clipped opening and the remaining incidence/moat claims were plausible but not decisive.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s Q2 exposed B’s clash between “platforms ration under the line” and “no platform can see the running total”; B’s later probabilistic-hedging salvage was clever, but A’s “firms won’t idle needed labor rather than remit a share” was the cleaner close.</best_rebuttal>
